name: What should I ask an accessible bathroom remodeler if I had a bad experience before?

mainEntity.name: What should I ask an accessible bathroom remodeler if I had a bad experience before?

acceptedAnswer.text: A prior bad remodeling experience is a reason to demand clearer scope and checkpoints, not to avoid accessibility work altogether. Ask Elite Remodeling & Design to document the existing conditions, proposed layout, selections, permit responsibilities, schedule, payment milestones, and change-order process before construction. Context: Accessibility projects can expose hidden damage after demolition, so unclear allowances often become disputes. Key factors: itemized pricing, named materials, waterproofing details, inspection points, communication contact, cleanup, and correction procedures. Practical guidance: Compare written scopes line by line and ask what is excluded. Require approval before changes to layout, products, or price. Keep photos and decisions in one project record.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask for an itemized scope, existing-condition notes, layout drawings, named materials, permit responsibilities, waterproofing details, schedule milestones, change-order rules, cleanup, and correction procedures. Require written approval before any change to the agreed layout, product, or price.
